outcome: Fix the two backend findings of the fifth round: semantic operations are serialized so that parallel tool calls from one agent cannot corrupt the shared SQLite and DuckDB connections, and a derive with a name and no expression is refused with the accepted shape and advice naming the aggregate route
criteria: Concurrent semantic operations from several threads and concurrent tool calls through the MCP server all complete without an INTERNAL error, shown by tests in tests/test_failures.py and tests/test_mcp.py that fail on the previous source

A derive entry with a name and no expression carries what was received and the fields in scope in details and returns derive_without_expression advice that names the aggregate route without a rewrite, shown by a test in tests/test_recovery.py, and the recorded qwen refusal of the fifth round replays with that advice
The full test suite passes, README Failure semantics names the new detector, and root README section 7 item 7 records that operations are serialized within one process

note: semantic_operation now takes the backend's re-entrant lock around every operation; a thread-pool test of 120 mixed operations and an asyncio.gather of 30 tool calls through the MCP server both produced INTERNAL InterfaceErrors on the previous source and pass now. The two derive refusals carry received, the accepted shape and the fields in scope in details; a bare name is reported as a name without an expression; the derive_without_expression detector explains what derive computes and that a value across rows is an aggregate step followed by a semi_join or a sort and limit, without a rewrite. The fifth round's recorded qwen refusal replays with that advice (23 of 23 recorded unadvised refusals advised, 18 of 18 rewrites succeed). README Failure semantics names the detector; section 7 item 7 records the serialization. Full suite green.
